newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: New deputy prosecutor named for Rwanda war crimes.
newsitem.headline: New deputy prosecutor named for Rwanda war crimes.

text.p: Bernard Acho Muna, a London-educated lawyer from Cameroon, was named deputy prosecutor for the Rwanda genocide tribunal, the United Nations announced on Tuesday.

Muna replaced Honoure Rakotomanana, a judge from Madagascar, one of two tribunal officials dismissed by Secretary-General Kofi Annan in February following a U.N. probe that found widespread mismanagement and financial waste.

Muna, 56, an attorney schooled in the French and British systems of law, served as head of the Central African Lawyers Union and was a prosecutor in Cameroon. He belongs to numerous international law groups and has published books and articles.

The tribunal, based in Arusha, Tanzania, with offices in the Rwandan capital of Kigali, is to try those alleged to be responsible for the slaughter by Hutu troops and militia of more than half a million Tutsis and moderate Hutus in Rwanda in 1994. A total of 21 people have been indicted.
The prosecutor for the tribunal is Louise Arbour of Canada, who is also prosecutor for the Hague-based U.N. tribunal on war crimes in the former Yugoslavia.

A report this year by Karl Paschke, the U.N. equivalent of an inspector-general, detailed administrative mismanagement, unqualified staff and legal chaos in the tribunal. The matter became the first test for Annan, who took office on Jan. 1 and is under pressure to reform the organisation and reduce waste and inefficiency.

Also named in the report was Andonico Adede of Kenya, who in effect served as chief administrator for the court. He was replaced in February by Agwu Ukiwe Okali of Nigeria, a graduate of the London School of Economics and Harvard Law School, who had served in the U.N. Habitat office in Nairobi.
That office recently also came under investigation for administrative irregularities.
